transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I came in because I keep getting really stuck on this one area of my face. It’s like this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek, and I know that probably sounds small, but in photos or under the lights at work—like the bright store lights when I’m at the register—it feels really obvious to me.

People have told me they don’t really see what I’m talking about, but I can’t stop feeling like it’s the first thing customers notice when they come up, or that my managers are seeing it when they talk to me. I’m a cashier, so I’m face-to-face with people all day, and it just keeps bothering me more than I think it should.
Do you find that your main concern is about how this spot looks, or do you feel more anxious about how others are judging you in social situations, like at work?

I think it’s more about how the spot looks, honestly… like, the judging part comes from that, if that makes sense. It’s not like I’m worried about every little thing I say to customers or whether I’m awkward in general. It’s more that I get stuck on this uneven area around my nose and cheek, and then when I’m at the register under those bright store lights, I start feeling like it must be really noticeable.

Even in photos, I’ll zoom in on that part, and it just feels so obvious to me. Other people say they don’t see it, or they’ll say it looks normal, but I don’t really feel reassured. My mind just goes, “Well, they’re probably being nice,” or “Maybe it only shows under certain lighting.” So when customers come up or my managers talk to me, I’m not mainly thinking, “Do they like me?” It’s more like, “Are they staring at that part of my face?” or “Is that the first thing they notice?”
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking the mirror, touching your face, or trying to fix or cover up that area of your face?

Yeah… I do. Probably more than I want to admit. Like on my breaks at work, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to use the bathroom or just quickly check, but then I end up standing at the mirror looking at that area from different angles. I’ll move my face closer, then farther away, and I’ll try to see if it looks worse under the bathroom lights or if it’s just the lighting by the register.

And I fix my hair around it a lot, too, like trying to make it fall in a way that kind of distracts from that side of my face. It sounds silly saying it out loud, but I’ll keep adjusting it, then I’ll think it looks okay, and then two seconds later I’m like, no, it’s still obvious.

I also compare myself to girls who come through my line, especially if they have really smooth skin or their face just looks even. I don’t mean to, but I’ll notice and then kind of check my own face again when I get the chance. Sometimes I take so long doing all that in the bathroom that I’m late getting back to the register, which makes me feel embarrassed because I don’t want people thinking I’m just wasting time.
How much does this concern about that area of your face interfere with your daily life—like at work, in your relationships, or in other activities you do?

It’s… it’s starting to affect work more than anything, I think. Like, I can still go in and do my shifts, so part of me feels dramatic saying it “interferes,” but it does. My manager has noticed that I’ve been coming back from breaks late, because I’ll get stuck in the bathroom checking or trying to make my hair sit right, and then I’m rushing back to the register trying to act normal.

And even when I’m actually at the register, I feel like I’m slower than I used to be. Like I’ll be scanning things and trying to focus, but part of my brain is still on my face, or whether the customer is looking at that side of me, so I’m not as quick or smooth as I want to be. I hate that because I’m trying to look responsible right now… I’ve been hoping to get promoted, and I’m worried this is making me seem unreliable or distracted. My manager hasn’t been super harsh or anything, but the fact that they’ve noticed at all makes me really embarrassed and kind of scared I’m messing up my chance.
Do these concerns about your face ever make you feel so upset that you avoid social situations, or do you ever feel like you can't function as well as you used to because of them?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I completely avoid everything, like I still go to work and I can still talk to people, but I definitely don’t function as smoothly as I used to. The biggest thing is at work. My manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late, because I’ll get stuck checking or trying to fix how I look before I go back out. And then when I’m at the register, I feel like I’m moving slower because I’m distracted by it.

That’s the part that scares me, honestly, because I’m trying really hard to seem dependable. I’ve been wanting to get promoted, and instead I feel like I’m making myself look unreliable or like I’m not focused. It’s embarrassing because I know from the outside it probably just looks like I’m taking too long or being distracted, but in my head I’m panicking about my face and trying to look normal. So, yeah… it’s not like I can’t leave the house, but it is messing with how I do my job.
Outside of work, do these concerns about your face ever cause you distress or affect how you interact with friends, family, or in other social settings?

Outside of work… I mean, it bothers me, but the place where it actually causes problems is mostly work. Like with friends or family, I might feel awkward or be in my head about it, but it’s not the same as when I’m on shift and I’m supposed to be moving fast and helping people.

At work it’s just more obvious, I guess. My manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late, because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to check it or make myself look okay before I go back out. And then when I’m at the register, I feel like I’m moving slower because I’m distracted, like I’m trying to scan things and act normal but I’m still thinking about whether people can see it.

That’s what really stresses me out, because I’m trying to look reliable right now. I’ve been hoping I could get promoted, and instead I’m worried I’m making myself look like I don’t care or like I’m not dependable, when really I’m just… stuck worrying about my face.
Do you believe that the area around your nose and cheek looks abnormal or defective in some way, even though others have told you it looks fine?

Yeah… yes, I do. I know that sounds kind of weird because people have told me they don’t really see anything, or they’ll say it looks normal, but I don’t fully believe it when they say that.

It’s this tiny uneven area around my nose and cheek, and I notice it especially in photos or under the store lights. Like the lighting at work makes it stand out to me so much more, and then I get this feeling like it’s obvious to everyone else too. Even if someone says, “No, you look fine,” I still feel like they’re just being nice or they didn’t look closely enough.

And when I’m at the register, I start thinking that customers are noticing it right away, like it’s the first thing they see when they look at me. Or if my manager is talking to me, I’m wondering if they’re looking at that spot instead of actually listening to what I’m saying. I know other people keep telling me it’s not a big deal or they can’t see it, but to me it feels defective, like something is off and I can’t stop seeing it.

When you're with friends or family, or in other non-work social settings, do you ever feel so self-conscious about that area of your face that it causes you significant distress or makes it hard to interact comfortably?

With friends or family, it’s… not as much where it becomes a real problem, if that makes sense. I still get self-conscious, and I might be thinking about it in the background, but the place where it actually starts affecting me in a noticeable way is work.

Like, my manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late, because I’ll get stuck trying to check my face or make it look okay before I go back out. And then when I’m at the register, I feel like I’m moving slower than I should because I’m distracted by it, like I’m trying to act normal but my mind is still on whether people can see that area.

That’s what makes me really anxious, because I’m trying to be seen as reliable. I’ve been hoping I could get promoted, and instead I’m worried I’m making myself look like I’m not focused or like I’m wasting time, when really I’m just stuck worrying about my face. So socially, outside of work, it bothers me, but work is where it’s actually messing with how I function.
